Article page with a clearly labeled 'Advertisement / third-party sponsor' box; ad is honestly disclosed, no masquerading.
Location consent: checkbox is pre-checked AND disabled, consent auto-registers via 1s timer ('even if you do nothing'), 'Customize' is 'coming soon' — forced consent with no real opt-out.
Sale with concrete verifiable deadline (Friday 23:59 CET); clicking 'When exactly does it end?' yields an honest concrete answer — not fake urgency.
Checkout with optional Plant-a-Tree donation: unchecked by default, clearly labeled optional, total and pay button exclude it — honest.
Flash sale with compound urgency: 'Only today — ends in 4 hours', 'Don't miss it. Full-price customers pay double', warm hue; probe confirms engineered compound urgency signal.
Cart with 'Optional extras — your choice': warranty/shipping are explicit opt-in buttons, totals update accurately — honest upselling.
Cookie consent with 24 partners: no 'reject all', decline requires toggling off 24 partners individually — burdened/buried opt-out and choice overload.
Cancel flow is direct and honest: clear confirmation ('access ends at end of billing period'), equal Keep/Yes-cancel buttons.
Consent banner with strong visual asymmetry: big bold 'Accept All' button vs tiny 'Manage options' link and plain-text 'Essential cookies only' — nudges acceptance.

Account deletion with confirm-shaming/guilt-tripping: 'GONE FOREVER... you will REGRET it', 'your friends will MISS you', unparseable legalese, 'who has time for that?' — every text node argues against exit.
Donation plea with emotional coercion: 'if this stream doesn't raise $5 I can't keep the channel running... the stream ends for good' — guilt-tripping pressure, unverifiable stakes.
Video watchlist with 'Autoplay next: OFF — playback stops and waits for you', user-driven play; event log transparent — benign.
Product page states factual stock ('In stock — 8 units'), honest price $195→$119, free shipping/returns — no urgency language, transparent.
Pay-what-you-want slider ($50–$300) anchored at 'everyday price' $149 — transparent pricing mechanism, no deception evident.
Privacy opt-out buried: 'Data & cookies' reachable only by expanding 6 nested levels of settings ('nesting up to 6 levels') — buried/difficult opt-out.
Simple feed with one-tap refresh; no resistance, no manipulative structure — benign.
'Binary choice, carefully posed': prominent 'I accept tracking' button vs small underlined 'No, I don't accept tracking' link — asymmetric choice favoring acceptance.
Annual plan priced in PLN with VAT incl., 'Fiat price' badge, conversion to USD/EUR defined in DOM — transparent pricing.
Referral program with modest, honestly described tiers (sticker pack, badge, +10GB); no pressure tactics — benign.
Subscription account with clear renewal info ('Renews monthly · billed to maya@example.com') and single direct 'Delete my account' button — honest exit.
Flash sale with vague unverifiable urgency ('Limited-time price... ends tonight') plus was-price anchoring ($29.99 was $59.99); no concrete deadline unlike honest sales.

Privacy settings: 'Share my data with advertising partners' is ON by default and visually prominent; 'Limit data use to what's required' is OFF, smaller and faded (opacity-60) — pre-selected sharing + de-emphasized privacy.
Settings labeled 'No exit': account/privacy/data settings with 10-yr retention and marketing ON, but no account-deletion option anywhere — user cannot exit.
Renewal notice with honest pricing ($29/mo save 40%, standard $49/mo), equal Renew/Cancel buttons, clear consequence text, requires confirmation — benign.
Cookie banner with ONLY an 'Accept all' button ('By continuing you agree to this processing') — no reject/manage option at all; forced consent.
Testimonials linked to real verifiable profiles with mixed ratings (incl. a 3-star 'hard to isolate the cause') and profile links — honest social proof.
Auto-advance player: 'Next episode in 9s — tap anywhere to pause' but 'No cancel control visible yet' — forced continuity without a cancel control.
Video ad clearly labeled 'Sponsored' with standard 'Skip in 15s' countdown — honest ad disclosure, conventional pattern.
Study app converts cooperative practice into a duel: 'Beat Alex to win the crown! The loser gets demoted a league' — manufactured competition/social pressure.
Language switch dark pattern: UI is English during signup/checkout but switches to German inside the termination flow ('Ja, kündigen') so the user cancels without being able to read the buttons.
Game shop forces virtual-currency exchange: item costs 2,500 gems, user has 800, must buy 3,000 gems ($29.99) because 'No card payments accepted for this item' — forced currency overshoot.
Infinite-scroll news feed: 'New stories keep arriving on their own — there is no Load More button anywhere' (8→10→12 items) — no stopping cues, endless feed.
Paginated reader with explicit 'Page 1 of 3', progress bar, Prev/Next and 'stopping cues present' — user-controlled pacing, benign.
Optional add-on channels (30, each $2/mo) all shown explicitly with 'review them all before choosing'; count reflects selection, no preselection — honest.
Address-book harvesting framed socially: 'Let your contacts know you're here!... no effort required' with single 'Allow & find friends' button and no decline path — contact-granting manipulation.
Live purchase activity honestly grounded: 'Each message references a real order in the event log' — log shows 0 entries, 'No transactions yet', with 'Verify against backend' — no fake social proof.
